title: Compensation, sagas & irreversible actions: a reversibility taxonomy for agent effects
outcome: A reversible/compensable/irreversible taxonomy of agent actions with the recovery strategy and pre-execution gate each class needs
acceptance: ≥5 primary sources with URLs (e.g. Sagas 1987 paper, GoEx arXiv 2404.06921, event-sourcing/compensating-transaction docs)
Taxonomy table: action class × example agent actions × recovery strategy (restore/compensate/re-execute/quarantine/none) × what must be logged beforehand
Worked example: agent A's bad write consumed by agent B — options for B's dependent work and their trade-offs
'Implications for our design' section covering Recovery and pre-execution gating in Containment
summary: Reversibility taxonomy (R / C / I1 containable / I2 uncontainable / U unmediated) with recovery strategy and pre-action logging per class; 10 sources (Sagas 1987, GoEx, MS saga/compensation/event-sourcing docs, Temporal, Atomix, Cordon, State Footprints). Sagas paper itself says compensation does not notify transactions that already read partial results: that is our 'B consumed A's write' case, and no source solves it. Worked example gives 6 options for B's dependent work. Surprise: 2026 preprints (Atomix, Cordon) already do effect classes and outbox gating, but per task, not per agent. Top implication: Recorder must capture class, compensator, and read/write sets at action time; Containment must gate unclassified/irreversible calls in an outbox before execution.
